items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: That era of people, it’s so great, they had such pride and like, who was that? Sugar Ray

ctx.x: Your father, and your mother, even though they were into music, still wonder about your choice. Did they have an attitude, pro or con, about jazz in itself?

No, they didn’t have a problem with jazz, because I was very lucky with them, I came from that era of black — there’s that word again — of black families, that stressed a couple of things you and I talked about before. First it was education. They come from that sort of Martin Luther King era where education is your way out, which they imparted that to me and it sticks with me and I still think, and as I study and try to help other people and help myself I realize that by increasing the quality of the product or…
